Signed positive-magnitude interpolation weights annihilate the perturbations at those nodes, proving optimality, uniqueness, and the converse for the ordered algebraic system. The remaining problem is to minimize the squared uniform norm of f(x)=x(1−x²)A(1−x²), x=√(1−y). The polynomial −(2/5)tan(π/10)T₅(x cos(π/10)) is in this family (odd, f(1)=0, f′(1)=−2), and its two opposite contacts on (0,1) certify optimality because every perturbation is a multiple of x(1−x²)².
